content: Projectile Motion (Class 11) Use tag projectile.html to show this visual. Projectile motion = object thrown at an angle under gravity only. Path is parabolic. Key terms: - Initial velocity (u) - Projection angle (θ) - Gravity (g) - Time of flight (T) - Maximum height (H) - Range (R) Motion components: - Horizontal: constant velocity - Vertical: acceleration due to gravity Velocity components: - uₓ = u cosθ - uᵧ = u sinθ Important formulas: - T = (2u sinθ)/g - H = (u² sin²θ)/(2g) - R = (u² sin2θ)/g Special cases: - Maximum range at θ = 45° - θ and (90°−θ) give same range Key observations: - Vertical velocity becomes 0 at highest point - Higher velocity increases height and range - Small angle → more range, less height - Large angle → more height, less range Interactive Animation: projectile.html Features: - Cannon fires projectile using adjustable angle and velocity - Real-time parabolic trajectory - Displays maximum height and horizontal range - Demonstrates horizontal and vertical motion components Teaching flow: - Change angle to compare height and range - Increase velocity to observe larger trajectory - Demonstrate maximum range at 45° - Compare complementary angles like 30° and 60° - Use trajectory to explain combined x-y motion
